# subtrack

Keep track of your subscriptions from the terminal: what they cost you each month, and what renews next.
Plain Node.js (ES modules), no dependencies.

```sh
subtrack add Netflix 12.99                        # monthly by default, first charge today
subtrack add "Domain name" 14 --every year --since 2026-03-02
subtrack list                                     # every plan with its monthly cost
subtrack total                                    # what all of it costs you a month
subtrack renewals --within 14                     # charges coming up in the next 14 days, soonest first
subtrack export > subs.csv                        # CSV for a spreadsheet
subtrack remove Netflix
```

During development, run it with `node bin/subtrack.js <command>`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--every month\|year` | add | How often the plan charges you (default `month`). |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | add | Date of the first charge (default today). Later charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month. |
| `--within <days>` | renewals | How far ahead to look (default 30). A charge today counts. |
| `--today YYYY-MM-DD` | list, renewals, export | Pretend today is another date. |
| `--file <path>` | all | Where your subscriptions are kept. Default: `$SUBTRACK_FILE`, else `./subscriptions.json`. |

## Money

Prices are typed in euros (`12.99`, `1,299.00`) and kept in whole cents. The monthly cost of a yearly plan is its
price divided by 12.

## Code

- `bin/subtrack.js`: the command line
- `src/cycles.js`: billing cycles: monthly cost and next charge of a plan
- `src/renewals.js`: upcoming charges
- `src/export.js`: CSV export
- `src/store.js`: reading and writing the subscriptions file
- `src/dates.js`, `src/money.js`: date and money helpers

Run the tests with `npm test`.

price divided by 12.

- `src/cycles.js`: billing cycles: monthly cost and next charge of a plan

- `src/export.js`: CSV export

content.text:
Weekly plans now work end to end, and monthly costs round to the nearest cent. All 41 tests pass. I haven't committed anything.

- **`--every week`** works next to `month` and `year` (`weekly` is accepted too). A weekly plan costs price × 52 ÷ 12 a month, so `€59.90` a week shows as `€259.57` a month in `list`, `total`, and the CSV export.
- **Charges every 7 days** from `--since`. Monthly and yearly charges work as before.
- **Rounding:** €119.99 a year now shows as `€10.00` a month. Costs are rounded half-up to the cent everywhere, using one calculation in `src/cycles.js`.

I made these changes beyond the three you listed:

- **CSV export** had its own copy of the monthly calculation, which would have ignored weekly plans. It now uses the same function as the rest of the app.
- **Loading a file** turned any cycle other than yearly into monthly, so a stored weekly plan would have silently become monthly on the next load. Only the old `month`/`year` names are converted now, and any other unknown name is rejected.
- **`renewals` sort order** compared the short labels as text, so "10 Nov" came before "2 Nov". It now sorts by date. This matters more with weekly plans.
- **Yearly rounding** changes one existing test: a €14.50 yearly plan now shows €1.21 a month, not €1.20.
- **README** covers the new option, the rounding rule, and a weekly example.

One choice for you to confirm: `renewals` lists each weekly plan once, with its next charge, like every other plan. It does not list each weekly charge in the window. Say if you'd rather see every upcoming charge.

I also ran your example commands against a scratch file, `/tmp/subtrack-check.json`. I couldn't delete it, since the cleanup needed approval, so you may want to remove it.
